original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Prove, for every address dimension n >= 3, that diag([c],[c]) for a coordinate 3-cycle c in M_2(F2[GL_n(F2)]) has no word of length at most 9, and reduce lengths 10 and 11 in every dimension to one five-coordinate case with explicit write/read profiles (Open next question 1 of PR #5379, research/spectator-three-cycle-additivity).
scope_change_reason: PR #5005 (n = 3) and PR #5379 (n = 4) settle the smallest cases by search; #5379 asks for every n >= 4 and names the missing written two-target argument as the blocker. A whole-word projection lemma supplies that argument for all but one residual case.
bottleneck_link: In this formal register model, extra address spectators cannot bring two 3-cycles below ten calls in any dimension; any further saving needs the residual five-coordinate word or a changed operation/tariff. No native implementation or kappa change follows.
stop_rule: Stop at the written all-dimension reduction with lemma checks. Do not search the residual n = 5 case in this package.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Do lengths 10 and 11 fail at n = 5 under the residual write profiles (6,4), (6,5), (7,4)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Excluding them gives exact cost 12 for two 3-cycles in every address dimension.
open_questions.first_step: Restrict a meet-in-the-middle search to words whose two spectators are each written and read at least twice.
open_questions.blocked_by: The unrestricted n = 5 ball over 120 paid letters is large; the profile restriction has not been implemented.

open_questions.question: Does the same reduction close a dirty third register with spectators, diag([c],[c],[e])?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Lemma 1 holds for any register count; combining it with R = 3 base cases would extend #5292 to every n.
open_questions.first_step: Recompute the write-count bound with the R = 3 rank condition.
open_questions.blocked_by: The R = 3, n = 3 length-11 case (#5292) is open and no R = 3 spectator base case exists.

open_questions.question: Does a two-write analogue of Lemma 1 force three writes per live spectator?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would remove the residual case without search.
open_questions.first_step: Classify when two writes to one row return it to the unit row inside the projected support.
open_questions.blocked_by: Two writes can cancel on the row, so the single-write projection no longer isolates one factor.
